newsitem.title: FRANCE: Nazi-hunters want Spanish-Portugese Nazi probe.
newsitem.headline: Nazi-hunters want Spanish-Portugese Nazi probe.

text.p: Simon Wiesenthal Centre Nazi hunters said on Tuesday they wanted an investigation into allegations that gold looted by the Nazis passed through Spain and Portugal to the Far East and Latin America.

Shimon Samuels, Paris-based director for Europe and Latin America of the Wiesenthal Centre, which has its headquarters in Los Angeles, said in a statement he had written to Bank of Portugal governor Antonio de Sousa and Bank of Spain governor Don Luis Angel Rojo Duque on the issue.
Samuels said he had "requested access to their archives on...gold transfers to Portugal and Spain in the period 1936-45, directly from Germany and/or indirectly via Switzerland.

"Likewise, documentation on such transfers from Portugal and Spain in the period 1945-1949, directly to Latin America and/or the Far East or indirectly via Switzerland and/or other countries," Samuels' statement said.

Argentina, which is trying to shake off an image as a haven for Nazi war criminals, recently opened up Central Bank archives for Jewish investigators trying to track down gold stolen from Jewish victims of the holocaust by the Nazis.

A secret U.S. document declassified two months ago, sent from the U.S. Embassy in Buenos Aires in April 1945, estimated the Nazis secretly sent more than $1 billion for investment in Argentina just a month before World War Two ended.
Samuel commended the Portuguese central bank for "its appointment of a history professor to investigate...the alleged and unexplained 1947 transfer of 15 tonnes of gold from Lisbon to Geneva."
But he also asked for open access to independent researchers rather than what he said was an analysis limited to in-house interpretation.
Samuels' statement came amid controversy between Jewish groups and Switzerland over Switzerland's own investigations into its financial role during World War Two.
